item.title: Can RayNeo’s smart glasses become a habit?
item.dc:creator: Lucia
item.description: Editor’s note: Founded in 2021 and incubated by TCL Electronics, RayNeo makes AR and smart glasses for entertainment, productivity and AI assistance. IDC ranked it second globally in AR/VR headset shipments in Q2 2026, with a 12% share. Its backers include early investors Fosun Capital and Winreal Investment, as well as China Mobile-linked funds and […]
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s note: Founded in 2021 and incubated by TCL Electronics, RayNeo makes AR and smart glasses for entertainment, productivity and AI assistance. IDC ranked it second globally in AR/VR headset shipments in Q2 2026, with a 12% share. Its backers include early investors Fosun Capital and Winreal Investment, as well as China Mobile-linked funds and CITIC Goldstone, with a China Unicom-affiliated fund participating in a D round exceeding RMB 1 billion in January 2026. The question now is whether RayNeo can turn its market traction into glasses people reach for every day.

A long flight, a hotel room or a wait between appointments can leave people looking for a bigger screen — or a way to check information without pulling out a phone. RayNeo’s latest lineup takes two different approaches: the minimalist iO, built around a small information display, and the maximalist GT series, which turns connected devices into a large virtual screen.

Two Ways to Wear a Screen

Launched internationally at IFA in September, the iO is designed to look like ordinary eyewear. At about 33 grams, it uses a small monochrome heads-up display for captions, live translation and prompts. Voice capture and AI features add meeting notes and reminders. The pitch is a light-touch assistant that can stay on throughout the day.

That puts iO in a different lane from camera-led glasses such as Meta’s Ray-Ban line. As Wareable noted, RayNeo is not positioning it as a direct rival to Meta’s camera glasses, but as a lightweight ambient assistant built around a small display and voice interaction.

The GT series takes the opposite approach. Designed for movies, games and work, the glasses connect to another device to create a large virtual screen. The GT Max can expand it to the equivalent of 307 inches, with spatial tracking and audio tuned by Bang & Olufsen. It is closer to a personal theater than an all-purpose computer.

A Tom’s Guide hands-on praised the GT Max’s comfort, while describing this category more accurately as “display glasses” — a wearable screen, not a self-contained AR computer. The GT’s job is to make a connected phone, laptop or console more immersive, not replace it.

The Bigger AR Ambition

RayNeo’s longer-term goal is more ambitious. Its X3 Pro, a standalone AI+AR model, weighs 76 grams and combines binocular full-color MicroLED displays with cameras, navigation, translation and AI. A TechRadar review praised its display but flagged its 245mAh battery and high price as major trade-offs.

Founder and CEO Li Hongwei has also pushed back the timeline for the category’s breakthrough. In a 2026 iFanr interview, he said AI had advanced faster than expected, while optical displays, chips and spatial computing had moved more slowly. His “iPhone moment” forecast has shifted from around 2025 to 2027.

Money for a Longer Race

Founded in 2021 and incubated by TCL Electronics, RayNeo has raised capital across multiple rounds. Its first external round, an A round of more than RMB 100 million in 2023, was led by Fosun Capital and Winreal Investment. Bilibili and Huatai Zijin later joined its investor base.

In January 2026, RayNeo raised more than RMB 1 billion in a D round co-led by China Mobile’s investment arm and CITIC Goldstone Investment, with a China Unicom-affiliated fund participating. D+ and D++ rounds followed in May and October, with amounts undisclosed.

Telecom backing could matter if glasses become independent connected devices: eSIM services, networks and distribution may prove as important as optics.

RayNeo has market momentum. Omdia ranked it second in global XR headwear shipments in the first half of 2026, with a 9.9% share. IDC later put it second in the broader AR/VR headset market in Q2, with 12%, and first in extended-reality glasses, with 25.2%. Meta led that broader market with 45.7%, according to IDC.

For now, RayNeo is pursuing two habits: wearing glasses for quick information throughout the day and putting them on for a big screen when there is time to sit back. Whether either becomes routine will matter more than how futuristic the hardware looks.

DragonLab cuts through the noise to find the Chinese startups, founders, and technologies that could shape what comes next.

item.title: Huawei Mate X8 hands-on video shows barely visible display crease
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: A leaked hands-on video of Huawei’s upcoming Mate X8 shows an inner display whose crease is barely visible from several viewing angles, IT Home reported Tuesday. The footage shows a glossy screen, while Huawei’s own teaser emphasizes improvements in display flatness. The company will unveil the book-style foldable on November 24. The Mate X8 has […]
item.content:encoded:
A leaked hands-on video of Huawei’s upcoming Mate X8 shows an inner display whose crease is barely visible from several viewing angles, IT Home reported Tuesday. The footage shows a glossy screen, while Huawei’s own teaser emphasizes improvements in display flatness. The company will unveil the book-style foldable on November 24.

The Mate X8 has also appeared on Huawei’s website in five colors, including purple, green, orange, black and white. Listed configurations range from 12 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage to a Collector’s Edition with 16 GB of RAM and 1 TB of storage. Huawei has yet to announce pricing. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: SenseTime releases open-weight Loop-9B model that reuses layers for deeper computation
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: SenseTime released the weights and code for SenseNova Loop-9B on Tuesday, a multimodal model that increases computational depth by running some of its layers more than once. The roughly nine-billion-parameter model accepts text and images, produces text, and supports reasoning, coding, data analysis and tool use. Its context window extends to 512,000 tokens. The model […]
item.content:encoded:
SenseTime released the weights and code for SenseNova Loop-9B on Tuesday, a multimodal model that increases computational depth by running some of its layers more than once. The roughly nine-billion-parameter model accepts text and images, produces text, and supports reasoning, coding, data analysis and tool use. Its context window extends to 512,000 tokens.

The model has 32 decoder layers, but executes its shared middle layers twice to perform 56 layers’ worth of computation in each forward pass. SenseTime says it is competitive with Qwen3.8-27B on selected agent and data-analysis benchmarks. An official four-bit quantized version reduces the weights to about 4.9 GB. Running it with a 256,000-token context and an eight-bit KV cache requires about 15 GiB of memory, according to the model documentation. [SenseTime]

The company announced the expansion on Tuesday following a launch event in Mumbai on November 13. The two models give Denza an initial lineup spanning luxury passenger transport and performance cars. The D9 is aimed at family […]
item.content:encoded:
BYD’s premium brand Denza has entered India with the D9 electric MPV and Z9 GT electric shooting brake. The company announced the expansion on Tuesday following a launch event in Mumbai on November 13. The two models give Denza an initial lineup spanning luxury passenger transport and performance cars.

The D9 is aimed at family and business buyers seeking space and comfort, while the Z9 GT targets customers looking for performance and technology features. The India launch extends BYD’s overseas expansion through a separate premium brand, bringing Denza’s flagship products into a market where the parent company already sells electric vehicles. [Gasgoo, in Chinese]

item.title: DJI raises Pocket camera prices in China as component costs climb
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: DJI raised prices for several handheld cameras and bundles in China on Wednesday, implementing the adjustment it announced last week in response to rising semiconductor, memory and other component costs. The Osmo Pocket 4 Standard Combo increased from RMB 2,999 to RMB 3,199, while the Pocket 4P Standard Combo rose from RMB 3,799 to RMB […]
item.content:encoded:
DJI raised prices for several handheld cameras and bundles in China on Wednesday, implementing the adjustment it announced last week in response to rising semiconductor, memory and other component costs. The Osmo Pocket 4 Standard Combo increased from RMB 2,999 to RMB 3,199, while the Pocket 4P Standard Combo rose from RMB 3,799 to RMB 4,099.

Some bundles saw larger increases. The Pocket 4P Vlog Combo rose by RMB 560 to RMB 4,859, and the Pocket 4 All-in-One Combo increased by RMB 500 to RMB 4,299. The 128 GB Osmo Nano also rose by RMB 200 to RMB 2,498, while the 64 GB model remained at RMB 1,998. The changes put specific prices behind DJI’s earlier notice, which had left the affected products and adjustment amounts unspecified. [MyDrivers, in Chinese]

item.title: Xiaomi takes its rear-screen flagship phones overseas, starting at €1,399
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Xiaomi launched the international versions of its 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max smartphones in Paris on Tuesday, bringing the series’ rear displays to overseas markets. European prices start at €1,399 for the 18 Pro and €1,599 for the Pro Max. The top Pro Max configuration, with 16 GB of RAM and 1 TB of […]
item.content:encoded:
Xiaomi launched the international versions of its 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max smartphones in Paris on Tuesday, bringing the series’ rear displays to overseas markets. European prices start at €1,399 for the 18 Pro and €1,599 for the Pro Max. The top Pro Max configuration, with 16 GB of RAM and 1 TB of storage, costs €2,099.

The rear screen displays calls, messages, navigation, music controls and travel information. Users can also create small AI-generated applications for it, including language-learning tools, exercise plans and games. Both phones feature Leica-branded cameras with 200-megapixel main and telephoto sensors. An on-device AI imaging feature offers CCD-style, monochrome film and contemporary camera looks, alongside simulated optical blur at 35 mm and 75 mm focal lengths. [IT Home, in Chinese]

The Beijing-based role covers developing the product from scratch, adapting playback and navigation for large screens, and exploring paid features such as casting memberships and subscriptions. The listing also calls for […]
item.content:encoded:
ByteDance is recruiting a product manager to build a television version of Hongguo, its free short-drama platform, according to a job listing reported Tuesday. The Beijing-based role covers developing the product from scratch, adapting playback and navigation for large screens, and exploring paid features such as casting memberships and subscriptions.

The listing also calls for coordinating content licensing and review procedures, building recommendations, search and viewing-history features, and connecting the television experience with Hongguo’s mobile app. Launched in 2023, Hongguo offers short dramas alongside films, television series, novels and audiobooks. The recruitment points to an expansion into living-room viewing, with the launch date and supported devices yet to be announced. [Phoenix Tech, in Chinese]

item.title: Kuaishou launches Kling Image 4.0 with native 8K generation
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Kuaishou launched Kling Image 4.0 on Tuesday night, adding native 8K image generation and the ability to produce up to 10 coordinated images from a single prompt. The model is also available through an API for developers and enterprise customers. It combines visual understanding and image generation in one architecture, targeting work such as advertising, […]
item.content:encoded:
Kuaishou launched Kling Image 4.0 on Tuesday night, adding native 8K image generation and the ability to produce up to 10 coordinated images from a single prompt. The model is also available through an API for developers and enterprise customers. It combines visual understanding and image generation in one architecture, targeting work such as advertising, storyboards and e-commerce design.

Kuaishou says the model can render up to 2,000 characters within a single image, with support for seven languages and more than 70 preset commercial fonts. Users can upload references to guide typography, lighting and color, or generate long images for product pages and website layouts. For multi-image projects, the model can plan the content of each image while maintaining a shared visual style. [Leiphone, in Chinese]

item.title: ZHITAI TiPro9000 review: a fast SSD that stays fast
item.dc:creator: TechNode Staff
item.description: We noticed the TiPro9000’s speed while editing. The clips were ready almost as soon as we brought them into the project. When we dragged the playhead across the timeline looking for a shot, the preview kept up. We tested the 2TB TiPro9000, a PCIe 5.0 SSD from ZHITAI, the consumer brand of Chinese NAND maker […]
item.content:encoded:
We noticed the TiPro9000’s speed while editing. The clips were ready almost as soon as we brought them into the project. When we dragged the playhead across the timeline looking for a shot, the preview kept up.

We tested the 2TB TiPro9000, a PCIe 5.0 SSD from ZHITAI, the consumer brand of Chinese NAND maker YMTC. It cut the wait for a game to start and made quick work of loading a local AI model. What stuck with us was how steady it stayed when we gave it a much longer job.

Less waiting, smoother editing

From clicking Launch in Cyberpunk 2077 to the first game logo, the TiPro9000 took about six seconds. A PCIe 4.0 SSD on the same testbed took about eleven, giving the TiPro9000 about a 45 percent reduction in waiting time at that step.

In video editing, importing 64 GB of footage shot at 50 fps took about two seconds. Preview playback was smooth, scrubbing through high-bitrate clips produced no stutter, and storage kept up during export. The experience carried through from bringing media into the project to working with it on the timeline, where interruptions can repeatedly break an editor’s concentration.

Loading a local AI model with 7 billion parameters took 1.52 seconds, about 14 percent faster than the same operation on the PCIe 4.0 drive. For someone switching models or restarting sessions, that saving recurs each time the model has to load. Together with the gaming and editing results, it gives a practical sense of how the TiPro9000 fits into a PC used for several kinds of demanding work.

Stays fast through large transfers

More than 5 TB into our continuous write test, the TiPro9000 was still writing at around 4.6 GB/s. The line on the chart barely moved. That’s the part you care about when you have a whole shoot to copy and the drive has worked through its fast write cache.

We ran the test in Iometer using 128 KiB blocks, a queue depth of 32 and sequential writes. The drive averaged 4,598 MB/s across about 5.52 TB of writes.

Cooling is part of that picture. Under high load, HWiNFO recorded an average composite temperature of 47 °C and a peak of 49 °C. The controller averaged 65 °C and peaked at 67 °C, remaining below 70 °C throughout the temperature test. Those readings accompanied a drive that also held its speed under prolonged writing.

The TiPro9000 comes with a removable heatsink made from dark matte metal, with angled fins for airflow. Its understated design suits the component’s practical role inside a case. Users whose motherboards lack an M.2 heatsink get cooling out of the box, while those with an existing motherboard heatsink can remove ZHITAI’s unit to fit their setup.

It gets close to its advertised speeds

We tested the M.2 2280 drive in a PCIe 5.0 slot on a Z790-E motherboard with an Intel Core i9-13900K. ZHITAI rates sequential reads at up to 14,900 MB/s and writes at up to 13,800 MB/s. After checking the drive in CrystalDiskInfo, we measured 14,261 MB/s for sequential reads and 13,025 MB/s for sequential writes in CrystalDiskMark, reaching about 96 percent and 94 percent of those respective ratings. The benchmark also recorded 4K random reads of 8,921 MB/s and random writes of 8,205 MB/s.

PCMark 10 and 3DMark added a view of performance through storage traces drawn from application and gaming activity. The TiPro9000 scored 6,428 in PCMark 10’s Full System Drive benchmark, with 985 MB/s of bandwidth and an average access time of 25 microseconds. In 3DMark Storage, it scored 6,100, with 1,029 MB/s of bandwidth and 29 microseconds of average access time. ZHITAI’s UNIMASTER utility provides a way to check drive information, health status and firmware version after installation.

The verdict

Saving a few seconds on Cyberpunk is nice. If you regularly come back from a shoot with a drive full of footage to move, the TiPro9000’s ability to keep a long transfer moving is the better reason to buy one.

Watch the full TechNode review on YouTube

item.title: Huawei’s new sub-brand OSTA set to launch first phone, reportedly featuring Kirin 9030S chip
item.dc:creator: Jessie Wu
item.description: Huawei’s smartphone lineup is about to welcome a new brand. Last week, Huawei announced its new sub-brand, OSTA (Xingmang), would make its public debut on November 20. Huawei said the brand aims to explore new possibilities in AI. OSTA is expected to focus on AI-powered smartphones, adding another category to Huawei’s existing smartphone lineup. Huawei’s […]
item.content:encoded:
Huawei’s smartphone lineup is about to welcome a new brand. Last week, Huawei announced its new sub-brand, OSTA (Xingmang), would make its public debut on November 20. Huawei said the brand aims to explore new possibilities in AI. OSTA is expected to focus on AI-powered smartphones, adding another category to Huawei’s existing smartphone lineup.

Huawei’s current smartphone portfolio includes the Mate, Pura and nova series. The Mate series targets the premium market, while Pura focuses on imaging and design, and nova is primarily aimed at younger consumers. OSTA, meanwhile, gives Huawei a new platform to explore AI smartphones and alternative device designs.

On Tuesday, the hardware specifications of OSTA’s first smartphone, the OSTA O1 Pro, were widely shared by Chinese tech bloggers. The device has already appeared on Huawei’s online store ahead of its launch and is expected to be unveiled this Friday.

Based on the leaked specifications, the OSTA O1 Pro’s biggest selling point is its adoption of a wide-screen straight-edge design and core hardware features previously found mainly in Huawei’s premium product lineup. At the same time, the company appears to have made compromises on certain secondary features to potentially bring the starting price down to around RMB 4,000 ($600).

Premium design could make wide-screen phones more accessible

The display is one of the OSTA O1 Pro’s most distinctive features. According to leaked specifications, the phone will feature a 6.39-inch 1.5K LTPS flat display with an unusual 16:9.5 aspect ratio.

Its bezels measure 1.05mm on all four sides, while the device is 6.68mm thick and weighs around 200 grams. Its overall design is highly similar to that of Huawei’s previously released Pura X View.

The key difference between wide-screen phones and conventional smartphones lies in their broader screen proportions, which offer a different look and feel in the hand, as well as a distinct viewing experience. However, such devices have so far been concentrated in Huawei’s premium lineup, with relatively high prices limiting their potential audience.

By bringing a similar display design to its new sub-brand, Huawei appears to be looking to make this form factor more accessible to consumers.

Kirin 9030S chip and 7,000mAh battery specifications

The OSTA O1 Pro is expected to be powered by the Kirin 9030S chip. This is one of the phone’s key hardware highlights. 

Although no performance test results are available yet, the choice of processor suggests that Huawei wants to retain flagship-level performance capabilities while keeping the overall cost under control.

The chip’s actual performance and thermal management inside the relatively slim chassis will be worth watching after launch.

The phone will also pack a large 7,000mAh battery and support 66W wired charging. Some versions are also expected to retain wireless charging.

Camera compromises include the removal of an ultra-wide lens

The OSTA O1 Pro’s camera system also reflects a series of trade-offs. The phone is expected to feature a 200-megapixel RYYB main camera with a 1/1.28-inch sensor, alongside a 50-megapixel RYYB periscope telephoto camera supporting 3.7x optical zoom. Huawei’s Red Maple imaging sensor will also be retained.

However, the device will reportedly drop the ultra-wide-angle camera entirely. This means users will have to rely on cropping from the main camera when shooting landscapes, architecture or group photos that require a wider field of view, potentially limiting the photography experience in certain scenarios.

The phone will also reportedly drop BeiDou satellite messaging, retaining only basic satellite paging capabilities. A side-mounted fingerprint sensor will replace the previous fingerprint recognition solution.

These changes reflect OSTA’s approach to cost control. The company appears to be prioritizing features such as the high-resolution main camera, periscope telephoto lens, flagship chip and large battery, while cutting back on some secondary functions to keep a more competitive price.

Can OSTA bring wide-screen phones to the mainstream market?

The OSTA O1 Pro’s product strategy is becoming increasingly clear. Rather than offering top-tier specifications across the board, it aims to make the wide-screen smartphone experience more affordable through carefully selected hardware trade-offs.

Huawei’s Pura X View previously launched at a starting price of RMB 5,999 ($900), while the OSTA O1 Pro is estimated to start at around RMB 4,000 ($600). The substantial price difference could give the new device a competitive edge if the expected pricing is confirmed.

Price alone will not determine its success. The actual performance of the Kirin 9030S, system optimization, camera capabilities and the impact of removing the ultra-wide lens on everyday use have yet to be fully assessed.

As the first product under the OSTA brand, the O1 Pro’s ability to attract consumers with its distinctive wide-screen design, Kirin processor and relatively affordable price will be one of the key things to watch at Huawei’s November 20 launch event.
